title: Why the son was looked down on
summary: Because of its black influence, light-skinned Cubans rejected the son, while charanga was seen as semi-classical European music.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Why was the Afro-Cuban son - ah - overlooked? Was there a reason for it?, why they were ignored or wanted to be?

No, because the - they had so much black influence. In those days, there was the beginning of the Republic of Cuba and everybody want to run away to have anything or any mixture with blacks. Everybody want to be white, so......
Even the Afro-Cuban wanted to be white?
I am talking about the mulato that passed for white.
The mula--- the the half-breed, the one that it was lighter.....

They want to be white so they refused to be, to accept, what the black people was doing. That was a second-rate, third-rate music. They don't want to be bothered. Charanga, it was almost a semi-classic thing. It come from the - they call it Charanga francesa, because the flute, the wood flute they was playing was originated in France and in England and it was a European instrument. That flute was used by the army to play a march to to create a gay atmosphere for the soldiers.
